title: The audit chain, and how you check it
summary: Every read, handoff, consent decision and erasure is appended to a hash-chained log. Verification is an operation anyone with the audit privilege can run - and it names the position where the chain breaks.

steps.label: Verify the whole chain
steps.note: Each record's hash covers the previous hash, so altering or deleting one breaks every hash after it. Verification recomputes the chain from the beginning; 'pending' counts rows that are appended but not yet sealed - outside the chain, not broken.

steps.label: Read the tail of the chain
steps.note: Positions, actions and hash links - no cid, no detail. Proving that the log cannot have been altered is a different privilege from reading what happened to whom: this credential holds the first and not the second.
